title: HEDP: A Hybrid Energy-Distance Prompt-based Framework for Domain Incremental Learning
claim: Naively reusing prior-domain knowledge, by adding clusters or prompts, blurs domain boundaries and causes confusion between domains.
layout: 2 stacked rows, before→after t-SNE pairs with arrows between, dashed divider
description: The figure has two stacked rows separated by a dashed line, each showing a pair of t-SNE scatter plots with a thick gray arrow between them. Row (a), 'Impact of Clusters', uses purple and cyan point clouds for domains A and B. Triangles mark cluster centers and stars mark samples. The labels 'add Clusters A' and 'add Clusters B' sit above arrows pointing in both directions. Dashed double-headed arrows show a sample's distances to nearby cluster centers. A domain B sample ends up closer to domain A's clusters. Row (b), 'Impact of Prompts', shows dense purple, cyan and gray clouds, each outlined by a dashed ellipse. The arrow is labeled 'add Prompts A'. After the arrow, the ellipses overlap heavily. A legend sits above each row, and bold captions sit below.
caption: t-SNE visualization of the feature space illustrating knowledge reuse challenges: (a) Impact of Clusters: simply adding cluster centers (triangles) creates ambiguous boundaries where samples from Domain B (cyan) are spatially closer to Domain A's clusters. (b) Impact of Prompts: optimizing single-domain prompts independently pushes distributions apart, creating overlap in the projected space that confuses the decision boundary.
abstract: Domain Incremental Learning is a critical scenario that requires models to continuously adapt to new data domains without retraining. However, domain shifts often cause severe performance degradation. To address this, we propose Hybrid Energy-Distance Prompt, a domain-incremental framework inspired by Helmholtz free energy. HEDP introduces an energy regularization loss to enhance the separability of domain representations and a hybrid energy-distance weighted mechanism that fuses energy-based and distance-based cues to improve domain selection and generalization. Experiments on multiple benchmarks, including CORe50, show that HEDP achieves superior performance on unseen domains with a 2.57\% accuracy gain, effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting and enhancing open-world adaptability. Our code is \href{https://github.com/dannis97500/HEDP/}{available here}.
